newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Feb 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - Feb 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- China Light & Power might have to delay the completion of Black Point power station under pressure from the government, which would cost billions of dollars.

-- MING PAO -- Chinese and British Foreign ministers would meet in Singapore on Friday to hold open and non-antagonistic talks. Sources said the British side would reiterate its opposition to the establishment of the provisional legislature.
-- Hong Kong elderly who went to live on the mainland were facing difficulties in receiving free medical care.

-- WEN WEI PO -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa said he hoped that all municipal councils and district board members could "love China and Hong Kong" and remain in their posts after the handover.

-- The total number of foreign currency deposits of Chinese residents exceeded US$30 billion last year. Most people held foreign currencies in fear of a renminbi devaluation and for preparing to go abroad.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- CITIC Pacific had arranged the largest syndicated loan in the territory's history, $12.5 billion, to finance the second part of its purchase of a 20 percent stake in China Light & Power.

-- The telecommunications watchdog OFTA was drawing up a new regulatory framework for broadband telecommunications, which was likely to cause a shift in relations between Hong Kong's telecommunications companies.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The Government was backing stock exchange moves to reduce dealing costs by abolishing the transaction levy, but was trying possible stamp duty cuts to appropriate cuts in broker commissions.
-- A senior official at the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Co-operation said China intended to adjust its policy on foreign investment in a bid to attract more capital.
